Connect to a zugodb database

Source: R/connection.R
dbConnect-zugodb_driver-method.Rd

Opens a connection to the driver's database. Two connections from the same driver share one database; dbConnect(zugodb(), dbdir = path) is the short form for a database of its own.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'zugodb_driver'
dbConnect(
  drv,
  dbdir,
  read_only,
  bigint = "numeric",
  threads = 2L,
  timezone_out = "UTC",
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'zugodb_connection'
dbIsValid(dbObj, ...)

# S4 method for class 'zugodb_connection'
show(object)

# S4 method for class 'zugodb_connection'
dbGetInfo(dbObj, ...)

Arguments

drv

A driver from zugodb().

dbdir, read_only

As for zugodb(). When either differs from the driver's, the connection gets a new driver, and so a database of its own.

bigint

How 64-bit integers (BIGINT, UINTEGER, UBIGINT) arrive: "numeric" (the default, as in duckdb), a double, with a value beyond 2^53 a zug_type_error; "integer64", the bit64 class; or "character", the decimal digits.

threads

The number of threads the engine may use, a whole number from 1. The engine has one thread pool per R process, so this is a cap for the whole process, not for this connection: the last dbConnect() sets it, and zug_info() reports it.

timezone_out

The time zone a TIMESTAMP column's POSIXct is shown in: "UTC" (the default, as in duckdb), another of OlsonNames(), or "" for the session's. The instant is the same in any zone; an unknown zone is an error.

...

Not used; an unknown argument is an error.

dbObj, object

A zugodb_connection.

Value

An object of class zugodb_connection.

Examples

con <- DBI::dbConnect(zugodb())
DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER)")
#> [1] 0
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
